title: Enterprise LLM Structured Outputs, Constrained Decoding & Large-Scale Tool-Calling Selection

tiers.tier: Tier 1: Prompt-Only `'Return Valid JSON'` + Regex / Markdown-Fence Stripping
tiers.architecture: Asking the LLM in the system prompt to output JSON without grammar constraints, plus dumping all 250 MCP tool schemas into every prompt

tiers.tier: Tier 2: Unconstrained Generation + Client Retry Loop (`Pydantic / Instructor` 3x Retries + All 250 Tools)
tiers.architecture: Catching `ValidationError` in Python and re-prompting the LLM with the traceback up to 3 times while still passing all 250 tools

tiers.tier: Tier 3: Naive Un-Cached FSM Constrained Decoding + Flat 250-Tool Context Dump
tiers.architecture: Compiling JSON Schema regex/FSM per request without FSM caching and still stuffing 45,000 tokens of 250 tool schemas into prefill

tiers.tier: Tier 4: Pre-Compiled Grammar-Constrained Decoding (`XGrammar / Outlines / Cloud Strict Schema`) + Top-8 Semantic Tool Router
tiers.architecture: Hierarchical Tool Router selects Top-8 relevant MCP tools (`45K -> 1.8K` tokens) + Pre-Compiled Pushdown Automaton / CFG Logit Mask (`< 0.5ms/tok`) + `Reasoning-First` Schema Field Ordering

scenarios.scenario: Eliminating Downstream JSON Parse Crashes (`81.4% -> 100.0%` First-Pass Schema Validity)
scenarios.question: An enterprise ERP integration requires the LLM to emit a 35-field nested order payload; prompt-only JSON fails on 18.6% of calls due to trailing commas, unescaped quotes, or missing required enums
scenarios.model_answer: Enable **Grammar-Constrained Decoding (`Azure OpenAI / OpenAI response_format={'strict': True}` for Cloud; `vLLM / SGLang + XGrammar / Outlines` for Self-Hosted)**: compiles the Pydantic/JSON Schema into a cached context-free grammar / pushdown automaton that masks invalid token logits at every decode step (`100.0%` first-pass schema validity, `0` retry loops!)
scenarios.tier1_3_failure: Tier 1 crashes downstream microservices on 18.6% of calls; Tier 2 hides the failures behind 3x retry loops that triple P95 latency to 3,420ms.

scenarios.scenario: Defeating the '250-Tool Context Bloat & Confusion Wall' via Hierarchical Semantic Tool Routing
scenarios.question: An enterprise Agent platform connects 250 MCP tools (45,000 tokens of JSON Schemas); dumping all 250 tools into every prompt drops tool selection accuracy to 54.5% and burns $110K/mo
scenarios.model_answer: Deploy a **Two-Stage Semantic Tool Router (`BGE-M3 / Hybrid Search` over tool descriptions + domain namespaces)** at the AI Gateway: dynamically injects only the **Top-8 most relevant tool schemas (`1,800 tokens` instead of `45,000 tokens`, -96% tool prompt bloat)**, lifting tool selection accuracy from `54.5%` to **`96.8%`** and cutting P95 latency to `380ms`!
scenarios.tier1_3_failure: Tiers 1–3 stuff all 250 tool definitions into every prompt, confusing the LLM across similar API names and wasting 43,200 prefill tokens per call.

scenarios.scenario: Preventing 'Premature Answer Lock-In' When Using Constrained JSON Decoding (`Reasoning-First Field Order`)
scenarios.question: When forced to output `{"verdict": "APPROVE" | "REJECT", "reasoning": "..."}` with `verdict` as the first JSON key, reasoning accuracy drops by 19 points!
scenarios.model_answer: Autoregressive models generate tokens strictly left-to-right: if `verdict` is the first key in the JSON Schema, the model must commit to `APPROVE/REJECT` **before** generating its chain-of-thought! Always order Pydantic/JSON Schema fields as **`{"step_by_step_analysis": str, "extracted_evidence": list[str], "final_verdict": Literal[...]}`**
scenarios.tier1_3_failure: Placing classification/decision enum fields before reasoning fields inside a strict JSON schema lobotomizes the model's reasoning quality.

scenarios.scenario: Avoiding First-Request Grammar Compilation Stalls in Self-Hosted `vLLM / SGLang` (`XGrammar` Cache)
scenarios.question: Compiling a complex 50-field JSON Schema into a finite-state machine on the fly adds 2–8 seconds of CPU compilation overhead on the first request
scenarios.model_answer: Use **`XGrammar` / `llguidance` byte-level pushdown automata with Pre-Warmed Shared Grammar Cache** in `vLLM / SGLang`: compiles schemas at CI registration time and executes token bitmasking on CPU in `< 0.4ms` overlapped with GPU kernel execution (`$27K/mo` TCO vs `$164K/mo` Tier 1, -83.5%)
scenarios.tier1_3_failure: Tier 3 recompiles uncached regex FSMs on worker threads during live traffic (`1,480ms` P95 latency).

perturbation_checks.check: Schema Evolution (`Adding a New Required Enum Field to ERP Payload v2.1`)
perturbation_checks.perturbed: 100.0% Validity (Pre-Compiled Grammar Cache Keyed by `SHA256(JSON_Schema)` Updates Instantly)

perturbation_checks.check: Ordering `final_decision` First vs. `reasoning_steps` First in Strict JSON Schema

key_findings: Tier 4 (Pre-Compiled Grammar-Constrained Decoding `XGrammar/Outlines/Strict Schema` + Top-8 Semantic Tool Router + Reasoning-First Schema Ordering) achieves 100.0% first-pass JSON validity and 96.8% tool selection accuracy across 250 tools at 380ms P95 latency and $27K/mo TCO (-83.5% vs Tier 1).

Dumping all 250 MCP tool schemas (45,000 tokens) into every prompt degrades tool selection accuracy to 54.5%–61.0%; routing the Top-8 relevant tools dynamically cuts tool prefill tokens by 96% and boosts accuracy to 96.8%.

In strict JSON Schema constrained decoding, always place `reasoning_steps` and `evidence` fields BEFORE `final_decision` / `classification` fields in the schema definition to prevent premature autoregressive commitment (+19.3 pts accuracy).
